findings.title: Potential OutOfMemoryError from large buffer allocation
findings.impact: A malformed or hostile AMQP message declaring a content length near Integer.MAX_VALUE (~2GB) causes OutOfMemoryError, denying service to the client
findings.evidence: Line 86-94: check `if(contentLength < Integer.MAX_VALUE)` permits allocation of arrays up to Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes, line 88: `final byte [] buffer = new byte[(int)contentLength];`

findings.title: Integer overflow in timestamp multiplication
findings.impact: Multiplying a long timestamp by 1000 can overflow the range when the input value is close to Long.MAX_VALUE, resulting in Date objects with incorrect or negative timestamps
findings.evidence: Line 269: `return new Date(in.readLong()*1000);` multiplies a long by 1000 without overflow checking

defects_to_look_for.mechanism: A length field read from untrusted input decides the size of a buffer, and that buffer is created before the corresponding payload has been shown to exist.
Decoding routines call one another in a cycle with nothing counting how deep the cycle has gone, so nesting in the input controls the depth.
